common_name: Cool Gold Piggyback Plant (Patented Golden Youth-on-Age)

planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted leaf plantlets in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in light to full shade; Cool Gold holds its color best out of direct sun, which scorches the thin gold leaves.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted leaf-base plantlets in spring or fall into consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in light to full shade, keeping the shallow roots from ever drying out. 'Cool Gold' is a patented sport of the Pacific Northwest native piggyback plant selected for fuzzy, clear golden-yellow foliage that holds its color far more reliably than older gold-splashed forms, which tend to revert to plain green over time. Like the species, mature leaves sprout a small plantlet at the base that roots wherever the parent leaf touches damp soil, so a single start multiplies quickly into a dense, low mat. Site it out of direct sun, which bleaches and scorches the pale leaf tissue, and in a spot with reliable moisture, since dry soil causes rapid wilting.

common_name: Black Style Yellow Wax Bells (Dark-Stemmed Kirengeshoma)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown specimens in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade, siting the clump where the near-black stems can be viewed against a light background.

directions: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade, and keep the root zone from ever drying out through summer. 'Black Style' is a selection of yellow wax bells grown chiefly for its dramatically dark, almost black stems and leaf stalks, which throw the large, palmate, maple-like leaves into sharp relief all season before the show shifts to flower in early fall. Pendulous, shuttlecock-shaped, waxy yellow flowers hang from the dark stems from September into October, later than most other shade perennials are still blooming, giving the woodland border a final flush of color. Because the stem coloration is most pronounced with a touch more light and cooler root conditions, avoid deep, dense shade that can mute the contrast, and mulch heavily to conserve the constant moisture this species demands.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown specimens in spring in rich, evenly moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial to full shade; avoid letting the root zone dry out even briefly during summer heat.

directions: Plant divisions or container-grown specimens in spring in rich, consistently moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial to full shade. 'Margarita' is a robust, upright, almost shrub-like selection of yellow wax bells with lime-green, hairy, maple-shaped leaves held on stems that darken to purple as the season progresses, a striking contrast to the foliage above. Nodding, waxy, sulfur-yellow bell flowers open at the stem tips from August through October, extending color deep into fall when most other shade perennials have finished. Its larger stature and stiffer, more architectural habit make it a good structural anchor at the back of a woodland border; mulch generously and water through dry spells, since it will not tolerate a parched root zone.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring in deep, cool, humus-rich, consistently moist soil in full to partial shade; like the species, 'Pink Kii' resents root disturbance and is slow to re-establish after division.

directions: Plant divisions in cool, deep, evenly moist, humus-rich soil in full to partial shade, enriched with leaf mold to mimic its native forest floor. 'Pink Kii' is a named selection of the Japanese false hydrangea originally collected on the Kii Peninsula, distinguished from the typical white-flowered species by clusters of rounded, light pink sepals opening from pink buds around a pale center in early summer. The bold, quilted, textured leaves form a slowly expanding clump that becomes more floriferous and attractive with age, so plants are best left undisturbed for years rather than divided frequently. Protect from drying wind and afternoon sun, and mulch to keep the root zone cool and constantly moist, since both drought and heat stress quickly show as leaf scorch.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or container stock in spring after the last frost in constantly moist, humus-rich, acidic woodland soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from strong wind.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in spring, once frost danger has passed, into constantly moist, humus-rich, acidic woodland soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from drying wind. 'Blue Blush' is a hybrid raised at Crug Farm Nursery in Wales from seed of Deinanthe caerulea pollinated by Deinanthe bifida, combining hybrid vigor and paler, bolder foliage with slightly larger flowers than either parent. Clusters of nodding, waxy, white blooms heavily flushed with blue open above the quilted leaves in mid to late summer, reading overall as a soft pale blue at a distance. Being part caerulea, it is somewhat more sensitive to heat than pure bifida selections, so give it a cool, humus-rich site that never dries out and avoid hot afternoon exposure.
